mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary conditions, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in >40% of cases when UNRATE increases by >0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by >5% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases by >2% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales suggests strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase by >1% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in >60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate combined with a simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp and FEDFUNDS increases by >0.1pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS increase as specified but S&P 500 returns are positive in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP increases by >0.5% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in >60% of cases.
